extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, draftsmen, and examiners preparing or reviewing patent drawings for USPTO (and PCT national stage) filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing, submitting, correcting, and formatting patent drawings for utility, design, plant, reissue, publication, and international (PCT) filings. Covers physical, content, and procedural standards required by 37 CFR and PCT Rule 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: View number formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: View numbers must be larger than the numbers used for reference characters. View numbers must not be used in association with brackets, circles, or inverted commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure view numerals are distinct and larger than reference characters and avoid using brackets, circles, or quotation marks with view numbers to prevent confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security markings are primarily the Office's responsibility; applicants may identify drawings with security designations (e.g., NATO, TS, S, or C) but should place them outside the usable drawing area, preferably centered in the top margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections must be durable and permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special correction products (e.g., white masking fluid) may be used if indelible and in compliance with other requirements; avoid non-permanent corrections that could affect reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not punch, drill, or otherwise create holes in sheets submitted as drawings to avoid reproduction and handling issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to specific drawing types
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of drawings: See § 1.152 for design drawings, § 1.165 for plant drawings, and § 1.174 for reissue drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific CFR sections for additional, type-specific drawing requirements; general requirements in §1.84 apply unless superseded by type-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must be corrected before examination (utility/plant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections to drawings are not held in abeyance; applicants must correct drawing objections promptly (in reply to Office drawing requirement) to avoid delay or abandonment and to be publication-ready for 18-month publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings filed after application may not be published
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.215(c), any patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submit drawings because late-filed drawings typically won't be included in application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not release drawings for correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction. If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the time set by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect to retrieve official drawings; prepare corrected replacement sheets and file them within the Office-set time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month time limit for corrected drawings after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected drawing is required or if a drawing does not comply with § 1.84 at the time an application is allowed, the Office may notify the applicant and set a three month period ... within which the applicant must file a corrected or formal drawing in compliance with § 1.84 to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month period is not extendable under §§ 1.136(a) or (b). Failure to timely submit corrected drawings can result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary post-allowance drawings may not be printed
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings voluntarily submitted by the applicant after allowance and payment of the issue fee may or may not be printed, dependent on the expediency of processing, provided an amendment to the brief or detailed description of the drawings to correspond to the new figure(s), if required, is also filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting drawings after allowance does not guarantee printing; include corresponding descriptive amendments and submit promptly if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing: description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of the operation and general content of computer program listings should appear in the description portion of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the function and content of any program listing within the written description rather than relying solely on the listing itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing size rules (<=300 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the computer program listing is contained in 300 lines or fewer, with each line of 72 characters or fewer, it may be submitted either as drawings or as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings <=300 lines can be included as drawings (complying with §1.84) or placed in the specification; each drawing sheet with a listing must have at least one figure numeral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing location in specification (>60 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any listing having more than 60 lines of code that is submitted as part of the specification must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large listings in the specification must appear after the description and before the claims; amendments to such listings must be made by substitute sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listings appendix requirements (>300 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any computer program listing having over 300 lines (up to 72 characters per line) must be submitted on a compact disc in compliance with § 1.52(e) as an appendix which will not be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CD (or Office-specified electronic medium) for very large listings; such appendices are not printed in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings (general and reissue/reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the application (or patent) drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval by the examiner, new drawings in compliance with § 1.84 including the changes must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed drawing changes require redlined sketches for examiner approval before filing formal replacement drawing sheets; in reissue/reexamination, amended figures must be labeled 'Amended', added figures 'New', canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency with drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain alignment between claims, specification text, and drawings; Office may require amendments to achieve substantial correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design drawings must comply with § 1.84 and be complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The design must be represented by a drawing that complies with the requirements of § 1.84 and must contain a sufficient number of views to constitute a complete disclosure of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all views necessary to fully disclose the claimed design; follow §1.84 general requirements unless 1.152 specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design drawing shading rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate and adequate surface shading should be used to show the character or contour of the surfaces represented. Solid black surface shading is not permitted except when used to represent the color black as well as color contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shading to convey surface shape; avoid solid black shading except to indicate true black/color contrast per the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design drawing broken-line and alternate-position limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may be used to show visible environmental structure, but may not be used to show hidden planes and surfaces that cannot be seen through opaque materials. Alternate positions of a design component, illustrated by full and broken lines in the same view are not permitted in a design drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use broken lines to depict hidden features; do not show alternate positions of components by mixing full and broken lines in the same view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design photographs vs ink drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and ink drawings are not permitted in one application. Photographs submitted in lieu of ink drawings in design patent applications must not disclose environmental structures but must be limited to the design claimed for the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose either photographs or ink drawings in a single design application; if using photographs, limit the image to the claimed design and avoid showing environmental or extraneous structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawings competency and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings should be artistically and competently executed and must comply with the requirements of § 1.84. The drawing must disclose all the distinctive characteristics of the plant capable of visual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure high-quality drawings or photographs that clearly show distinctive botanical traits; examiner may not require view numbers/reference characters unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant color requirement when distinguishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings may be in color. The drawing must be in color if color is a distinguishing characteristic of the new variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color is claimed as a distinctive trait, submit color drawings/photographs. Historically a black-and-white photocopy was required, but a waiver has been noted (check current practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawing reproduction and photo finish guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Two copies of color drawings or photographs and a black and white photocopy that accurately depicts, to the extent possible, the subject matter shown in the color drawing or photograph must be submitted. (WAIVER noted: black/white copy may not currently be required.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting color images, include required copies per current Office guidance and check for waivers or updated requirements regarding black-and-white photocopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawing content and completeness (show distinctive characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings must show the most distinguishing characteristics of the plant. Care should be taken to assure that the subject is well centered and clearly in focus. Drawings should avoid inclusion of superfluous information or materials such as tags or stickers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict all distinguishing botanical features, center and focus subjects, avoid extraneous items; may include rulers or scale where helpful; photography should not be retouched or color-amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawings: depict whole plant plus parts and seasonal variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should not be limited to a single plant part but should also depict the entire plant; distinguishing characteristics occurring at different seasons should be illustrated and may be depicted in different sheets or figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include whole-plant views and supplemental close-ups for specific parts; show seasonal states (e.g., dormant for deciduous perennials) and multiple stages (bud, early bloom, late bloom) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawings: supplemental close-ups when scale insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where flowers, foliage, fruit, etc. of the claimed plant are not depicted in sufficient scale in a whole plant drawing or view, this view should be supplemented with a close-up view of specific parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide magnified views for small but distinctive parts so detail remains visible even after possible 50% reproduction reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawing scale and reduction clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should be of such scale and clarity that necessary detail can still be discerned even with a fifty percent reduction in scale as may happen upon printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose drawings with sufficient line weight, contrast, and detail to survive typical reproduction reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawing examples of required supplemental views
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Ornamental flowering plants — views at bud, early bloom, and late bloom; Fruit/nut bearing plants — views depicted at different attitudes, with fruit split in different directions to show details and coloration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow botanical practice in showing relevant developmental stages and internal structures (e.g., seeds, stone, flesh coloration) where these are needed to claim distinctiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant drawing pedigree and fingerprint presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the pedigree of the plant is disclosed in the form of a detailed flow chart, this must be made a drawing view and not appear in the specification. Fingerprint information may also be presented as a figure of the drawing and should include identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place pedigrees and fingerprint/isozyme banding illustrations among the drawings (views), not in the descriptive text; ensure such figures are formatted as drawing sheets with view numbers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of drawing views limited to minimum necessary (plant)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of drawing views (and sheets) in plant patent applications should be limited to the minimum number necessary to adequately depict the distinctive botanical characteristics of the claimed patent which are capable of being visually represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide only the views needed to disclose the plant clearly; the Office examines drawings for content, detail, scale, and color fidelity, and informal/single copies will delay prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application drawing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must contain the entire specification, including the claims, and the drawings of the patent. No new matter shall be introduced into the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit clean copies of each drawing sheet of the printed patent when filing a reissue; if changes are to be made, follow the redline sketch/approval/new-drawings process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of amended/new/canceled figures (reissue/reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' any added figure must be identified as 'New.' In the event that a figure is canceled, the figure must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit labels for any drawing changes in reissue or reexamination proceedings to clarify status of figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requires drawings in compliance with §1.84
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may delay publishing any application until it includes ... drawings in compliance with § 1.84. The patent application publication will be based upon the application papers deposited on the filing date ... drawings in compliance with §1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings comply with §1.84 at filing (or timely amended copies submitted under §1.215(c)) if you want them included in pre-grant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) drawings must be present at filing to preserve date
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawings are necessary for the understanding of the invention, or are mentioned in the description, they must be part of an international application as originally filed in the United States Receiving Office in order to maintain the international filing date (PCT Art. 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required drawings at initial international filing; missing drawings may be accepted if received within 30 days of first receipt of incomplete papers, otherwise references to drawings are considered non-existent.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 fitness for reproduction and sheet condition
rubrics_metrics.description: All elements of the international application shall be so presented as to admit of direct reproduction ... All sheets shall be free from creases and cracks; they shall not be folded. Only one side of each sheet shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare PCT drawings on uncreased, unfolded single-sided sheets suitable for direct photographic or electrostatic reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 material and sheet size
rubrics_metrics.description: All elements of the international application shall be on paper which shall be flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny and durable. The size of the sheets shall be A4 (29.7 cm × 21 cm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A4 or Office-accepted equivalent paper that meets the stated material qualities; if other sizes are accepted, record/search copies must be A4.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 margins and usable surface
rubrics_metrics.description: On sheets containing drawings, the surface usable shall not exceed 26.2 cm × 17.0 cm. The minimum margins shall be: top 2.5 cm; left side 2.5 cm; right side 1.5 cm; bottom 1.0 cm. The margins must be completely blank (except limited top-left applicant file reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep drawing content inside the usable area; leave required blank margins and place any allowed applicant file reference within 1.5 cm of the top in the left corner, limited to the Administrative Instructions' character count.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 numbering and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: All the sheets contained in the international application shall be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals. The numbers shall be centered at the top or bottom of the sheet, but shall not be placed in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number sheets centrally at top or bottom (not in margins) using Arabic numerals for ease of reproduction and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11: words in drawings limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings shall not contain text matter, except a single word or words, when absolutely indispensable ... Any words used shall be so placed that, if translated, they may be pasted over without interfering with any lines of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize text in drawings to only indispensable catchwords (e.g., 'water', 'open'); place them so translations can be pasted over without damaging lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 alterations and erasures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet shall be reasonably free from erasures and shall be free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Non-compliance may be authorized if authenticity is not in question and reproduction is not jeopardized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid corrections and overwrites on drawing sheets; if unavoidable, ensure authenticity and reproduction quality remain intact and seek Office authorization when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 11 special requirements for drawings (line quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be executed in durable, black, sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined, lines and strokes without colorings. Cross-sections shall be indicated by oblique hatching which should not impede the clear reading of the reference signs and leading lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solid black, uniformly thick lines for clarity in reproduction; cross-hatching should be legible and not obscure reference numbers or leader lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: flowsheets and diagrams are drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Flowsheets and diagrams are considered drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include flowcharts and block diagrams among drawings and conform them to the physical and content drawing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: time limits for filing additional drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 7(2)(ii) shall be reasonable ... and shall, in no case, be shorter than two months from the date of the written invitation requiring the filing of drawings or additional drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a designated Office requires additional drawings under PCT, expect at least a two-month minimum period to supply them; check the specific invitation for the exact deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: abstract may be accompanied by a figure
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should indicate the number of the figure of the drawings which the applicant suggests should accompany the abstract when the abstract is published; in exceptional cases applicant may suggest more than one figure. The ISA may indicate a different figure or no figure if none are useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest a figure to illustrate the abstract when filing; the International Searching Authority or International Bureau may select or omit a figure based on usefulness for the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: expressions/drawings not to be used
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall not contain expressions or drawings contrary to morality or public order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including offensive, immoral, or public-order-contrary text or images in any part of the international application, including drawings.
